note.explanation: Biomolecules are molecules made by organisms. They help build cells and carry out life processes. Metabolism includes all the chemical reactions in an organism: anabolism builds complex substances, while catabolism breaks them down.
examples: Proteins make up 50% of the dry mass of protoplasm.
Anabolism combines simpler substances to form complex substances.
note.checkAnswer: Catabolism breaks complex molecules into simpler ones and releases energy.
note.simple: Cells contain different kinds of large molecules. Some provide or store energy, some build cell structures, and some carry genetic information. The chemical reactions happening in an organism are called metabolism.

explain.title: What biomolecules are
explain.body: The molecules produced by organisms are called biomolecules or biological molecules. They include carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids (DNA and RNA). They are mostly large in size and are called macromolecules.

explain.title: Where they are found and what they do
explain.body: Biomolecules occur in different cell locations and have different roles. Carbohydrates provide and store energy; proteins can act as enzymes, form structures, and control cellular traffic; lipids store energy, insulate against heat, and form part of cell membranes. DNA carries genetic information, while RNA carries information from DNA to ribosomes for protein synthesis.

explain.title: Biomolecules in dry mass
explain.body: Biomolecules make 93% of the dry mass of protoplasm. The remaining 7% comprises vitamins and inorganic substances. Of the listed biomolecules, proteins make up 50%, nucleic acids 18%, carbohydrates 15%, and lipids 10%.

explain.title: Metabolism
explain.body: All the chemical reactions that occur in an organism are collectively called metabolism. Anabolism combines simpler substances to form complex substances and uses energy. Catabolism breaks complex molecules down into simpler ones and releases energy.

explain.title: Biochemistry and molecular biology
explain.body: Biochemistry is the study of the chemical processes that occur within living organisms. Molecular biology is the study of the structure and function of the biomolecules.

mistakes: Do not confuse anabolism with catabolism: anabolism builds complex substances, while catabolism breaks them down.
Do not say that anabolism releases energy; it uses energy, whereas catabolism releases energy.
Do not mix up the dry-mass percentages: proteins are 50%, nucleic acids 18%, carbohydrates 15%, and lipids 10%.
Do not confuse the role of DNA with that of RNA: DNA carries genetic information, while RNA carries information from DNA to ribosomes for protein synthesis.
